events.title: Act of Union Merges the Canadas
events.description: On July 23, 1840, the British Parliament passed the Act of Union. It abolished the separate legislatures of Lower Canada and Upper Canada and joined them into a single Province of Canada.
events.significance: The act reshaped British North America and set the stage for later debates over self-government and Confederation in 1867.

events.title: Birth of Haile Selassie
events.description: Tafari Makonnen, who became Emperor Haile Selassie I of Ethiopia, was born on July 23, 1892. He ruled Ethiopia for decades and died in 1975.
events.significance: He became a global symbol of African independence. He also remains a revered figure in the Rastafari movement.

events.title: Ford Motor Company Sells Its First Car
events.description: Just weeks after it was founded, the Ford Motor Company sold its first automobile on July 23, 1903.
events.significance: This modest sale was the start of a company that went on to put the automobile within reach of ordinary families and reshape modern industry.

events.title: Chinese Communist Party Holds Its First Congress
events.description: On July 23, 1921, delegates met in a house in Shanghai to open the first National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party.
events.significance: The small gathering launched a movement that would eventually govern the world's most populous nation.

events.title: Telstar Beams Television Across the Atlantic
events.description: On July 23, 1962, the Telstar satellite relayed the first live television signal between North America and Europe.
events.significance: It opened the era of satellite communications and made live global broadcasting possible.
